title: SRD coverage: lycanthropes, pre-materialized in their hybrid forms
summary: The five lycanthrope identities, built per issue #43's decision as concrete creatures rather than an applied template. Each record is the hybrid combat form — the shape a GM actually runs a fight against — with the human life bought as an Alternate Form, so the two-shaped identity is priced instead of narrated. The curse itself is not a point value: a bite that breaks the skin may pass it on, and that is an affliction the campaign adjudicates, not the creature's character sheet. Silver is handled the same way the swarms handle what the rating cannot see — regeneration is priced from the published table, and the stat notes state plainly that wounds dealt by silver do not close.

monsters.name: Werebear
monsters.lair: A cabin or cave a long way from a road, kept by someone who moved out there for everyone else's sake.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Bear-sized, on a reasoning creature's aim.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: A bite that breaks the skin can pass the curse; werebears know it, and bite only what they mean to kill or keep.

monsters.description: The one lycanthrope that mostly chose this. Werebears keep the shape on purpose and keep away from people on purpose, and the thing standing in the forest track is usually working out whether the party is a problem for the valley it looks after. If it decides they are: a head over a big man, four times the weight, and cleverer than the bear it resembles.
notes: Wounds dealt by silver do not regenerate.
provenanceNotes: Hybrid form throughout; the human life is the Alternate Form. The animal form's numbers sit between the two and are left to prose.

monsters.name: Wereboar
monsters.lair: Rough farmland or scrub hills, at the end of the lane the neighbors stopped using.

attacks.name: Tusk Gore
attacks.notes: Delivered on a charge when it can get one; the second gore is for whoever helps the first one up.

attacks.name: Fists
attacks.notes: A bite that breaks the skin can pass the curse.

monsters.description: Belligerence with tusks. Wereboars do not stalk and do not scheme. They take offense, charge, and keep charging until something stops being upright. The ones with families pass the curse along like a surname, and a pair on their own ground fight as though they have stopped counting wounds, because they have.
notes: Berserk is the identity. Hurt one and it stops defending, and it stops retreating as well.
Wounds dealt by silver do not regenerate.

monsters.name: Wererat
monsters.lair: Cellars, sewers and warehouse lofts in any city big enough to lose things in.

attacks.name: Shortsword
attacks.notes: Wererats fight with tools, in numbers, from behind.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Filthy, and it knows it: the wound sickens, and a bite that breaks the skin can pass the curse. Wererats bite people they want in the family.

monsters.description: The curse run as a criminal enterprise. Wererats recruit, and a nest is a gang — pickets, escape holes, a ledger, and a rule about not killing anyone the city would miss. Four turn up in the alley. Those four are the ones the nest could spare.
notes: Wounds dealt by silver do not regenerate.
provenanceNotes: The smallest and most organized of the line; the appearing number is a patrol from a larger nest.

monsters.name: Weretiger
monsters.lair: A solitary hunting range with one comfortable den, kept the way a fastidious person keeps a house.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Both hands, faster than a fencer.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Aimed at the neck of whatever the claws opened. A bite that breaks the skin can pass the curse; weretigers consider that carelessness.

monsters.description: A hunter as calm as the tiger it becomes. Weretigers work alone, choose their prey days ahead, and treat the curse as an inheritance to be lived up to. The fight happens where the weretiger wanted it, and the first anyone knows of it is that it has already started.
notes: Wounds dealt by silver do not regenerate.

monsters.name: Werewolf
monsters.lair: A den within a night's run of a village, and a bed in that village the rest of the month.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: The famous one. A bite that breaks the skin can pass the curse, and the werewolf in the grip of the moon is not choosing carefully.

monsters.description: The classic curse: an ordinary person most of the month and this the rest of it. A werewolf pack is part family and part affliction, running the hills around a settlement that has started counting its dogs. Silver is not a rumor. Bring some, or bring rope.
notes: Wounds dealt by silver do not regenerate.
provenanceNotes: Bestial carries the moon-driven judgment: in hybrid form its problem-solving is a wolf's, whatever it remembers being on Tuesday.
